exit 0 Hi Eli, When the taxonKey column contains pipe-delimited values, it means that the taxon has been mapped manually. If the trait data set has a higher taxon that is not represented in our hierarchy, we map it to all the subgroups that are contained within that higher taxon. Sorry, I have not yet gotten around to adding the taxonMap column to the Brusca file to indicate manual mappings. It would probably be a good idea to include a rule in your name matching script to not skip taxa with pipes in the taxonKey column, even if the taxonMap column is missing or empty. Thanks for checking, Katja ---------------- Ah yes, I forgot. If there are no ancestry or higherClassification fields, we should not try to map automatically.
